Episode 247. Liberation War of Lafrarosa (10)
'Is that Kri...'
Jin, Murakan, and the Battle Kings also looked up at the sky.
Kri, originally a red air fortress symbolizing the Red Plutonian, was now covered in chaotic energy like tumors sprouting all over its hull.
This made it look even more dangerous, reminiscent of the giant ship 'Ram' operated by the Evil God during the old times.
'I should assume it's even more powerful than Ram.'
Gooooo...!
A massive dark wave energy, never before seen in the great desert, was emanating from Kri.
Even without seeing its power source directly, anyone could tell. It was as if infinite power was vibrating deep within that mountain-like hull, like the sun.
Just the fluctuation of its power was enough to split the earth and warp the sky. A terrifying power capable of erasing a continent was bound to a single air fortress.
"My people, snap out of it! Our final battle cannot be tainted like this."
Despite Shimat's desperate cry, the Red Plutonians didn't respond.
Those who survived were already consumed by chaotic energy. They were no longer his loyal brothers, but expendable tools of chaos.
The dying Grand Battle Kings were no different. They were now clinging to the air fortresses, their torn flesh and bones healed with chaotic energy.
[Gaaaaah.]
[Guuuuh...!]

Bakarun was fused to the central part of Pibil, while Rakiman and Bekios merged with the upper parts of Bessel and Rital. It was as if someone had randomly torn them apart and stuffed them into the damaged parts of the air fortresses.
Shimat felt a surge of nausea at this grotesque sight.

The fact that his people had become flesh of chaos was driving Shimat to despair, even more than Jin's overwhelming power or the inevitable future of destruction. Only the empty eyes of his people, stained with chaos, were left.
"Lokia Ganesto. How dare you, what are you... doing."
[If only you had done what you were supposed to do, Shimat. Then neither of us would have had to go through all this trouble.]
Ziiiing!
Suddenly, a giant red spear emerged above Kri. The face of Lokia, hidden under the hood, appeared within the spear.

[But now, at least, a satisfactory outcome has been reached, so it's something to be commended. You've worked hard. Now you can rest easy. You can let go of the lifeline forcibly held by the power of Genesis, or else...]
A main cannon protruded from the center of Kri. The speed was so fast that even Shimat almost missed it, and the cannon immediately spat fire at him.
The blast of chaotic energy and dark energy, Shimat quickly swung his sword, but unlike other air fortresses, this wasn't an attack that could be fended off.
"Cough!"
Even a body made of dark energy couldn't avoid the impact of the attack. He was completely engulfed in the bombardment for a while, convulsing.
The chaotic energy in the bombardment devoured him like a swarm of insects.
[I could end that pathetic life of yours. A kind of consideration, perhaps? A reward for a dog that barked well in the end.]

This was different from wounds inflicted in a fight between warriors, sword against sword. It was different from the powerlessness felt in battle. The main cannon of Kri, tainted with chaos, was thoroughly trampling on his last pride.
With every bit of chaos that entered his body, he heard the screams of his people.

The ancient times of ruling as a sovereign, the inevitable fate as a great seal, the humiliation of being used by insignificant humans, and now, facing destruction again even after regaining the Battle God.
All the despair and frustration of his people were lacerating Shimat’s inner self. Sharp fragments of shattered dreams.
"Leave my people to die, Lokia Ganesto. If you don't want to regret it."

[Oh, how scary. Let your people just face death? Haha, such words coming from your mouth. You've used the lower ones as expendable all this time. While operating an immortal army, you squeezed every last bit out of those who should have been allowed to rest.]
As Lokia spoke, the blast from the bombardment subsided.
Where Shimat had been standing, there was now a gigantic hole, its depth unfathomable. The blackened sands of the desert were sucked into the vortex like water.

Shimat, looking almost like a mere skeleton, barely managed to avoid falling into the center of the whirl, spreading a dark wave energy around him. The chaos clinging to his body like leeches continued to gnaw away at him.
"I said to let them die."

[And didn't you say the same to my descendants? The Red Plutonian doesn't hesitate to trample on the weak, and isn't afraid to be defeated by the stronger. Then, Shimat, this is just such a situation. It’s not just Jin; someone stronger than you has appeared and is merely using your underlings at will.]
Swoosh!
Tetallon unleashed a red sword energy towards Kri. However, the energy couldn't even reach near Kri, blocked by the protective shield formed by the four air fortresses.
It wasn't because he was weakened by the bombardment. Even while fighting Jin, he had pierced through the Plutonian Domination Sword several times, inflicting shallow wounds on Jin's body.

The reason Tetallon couldn't reach Kri now was that his inner self was shaken. The fact that he could no longer fight with his last pride, that all of this was a result of his own mistakes, was blurring his sword.
- You are just a foolish leader who led yourself and your people into chaos, into the jaws of chaos. If you could die intact, it would be fortunate for your people.
It was just as Jin had said earlier. He, not Lokia, had turned his people into flesh of chaos.
If he had not joined hands with chaos.
If he had not used, or even accepted, the orb given by Lokia, would the outcome have been different? Could he have died fighting as a Red Plutonian, not as a monster infected with chaos?
Regret flooded in every time he blinked. His legs were staggering, caught in chaos.
"Jin Runcandel."
Suddenly, Shimat called out to Jin. He did not turn around.
"I finally understand why the old man, the Blue Wind Emperor entrusted you. Our fight... ends here. I acknowledge my defeat. You surpass me as a warrior and are incomparably superior as a leader."

Creak, crack, sizzle...! The chaos clinging to Shimat began to melt away. His emaciated body did not return to normal, but his real body had turned to ash long ago. He had been able to fight even without a physical body for a while now.

"It may seem trivial, but I want to use my last moments for my people. From now on, I will fight with my back to you. I will cut down that witch's follower, our greatest pride, the air fortress. Even if you stab me in the back, I will accept it."
Jin did not respond.
There was no need to dissuade him. For the next twelve hours, whatever happens, Lafrarosa must be protected.
[You don't think that merely this atones for your sins, do you, Shimat? How inappropriate for you to have such shining eyes.]

"I can never be forgiven for the sins I have committed against my people. So, my people, listen. I will grant you death. I will bear all this pain and chaos on your behalf. Even if I cannot find rest, at least you must."
The inner chaos tormenting Shimat faded away.
The despair and resentment of his people still echoed within him, not entirely gone. Rather, those voices of grudge became clearer and amplified with each passing second.
It was a pain that could never be overcome.
Yet, he had to keep moving and fighting, even if shrouded in darkness. He had to find a way, even if blind, a way for his people to find peace.
Lokia, observing Shimat's inner turmoil, was laughing.
[It's amusing. To seek hope in rest after living such a bloodstained and terrible life. And that too, just because of one awakening, just for fighting desperately once. Isn't that right, descendant?]
Lokia easily repelled Shimat's approach, as if swatting a fly. Every time Kri's main cannon fired dark energy, Shimat was plunged deep underground, together with the chaos.
Continuous bombardments prevented him from escaping the pit, even as Shimat's sword burned red again.
From within his hood, Lokia's shimmering eyes met Jin's for the first time.
And Jin felt it. As soon as their gazes met, Lingling, hidden in the depths of his heart, screamed.
"You're trying hard to sever the connection between me and Sister Vahn, Lokia Ganesto. Don't dare call me your descendant with that filthy mouth."
[It's disappointing. Without me, you wouldn't have existed. How many times did I save the life of Temar before he had children? Didn't Murakan tell you about that?]

[Lokia. You... indeed, you're not the person I knew. Even though you had crossed the line since a thousand years ago, everything you did was for Temar and the family. But what did you gain by betraying us? What exactly is your purpose?]

[You're asking the obvious. My purpose, then and now, is only one. I've said it many times, I want a correct world. That's why I was drawn to Temar. At least he, for a time, seemed like he could really change the world... far more radiant than the kid beside you now.]
Murakan let out a dry laugh.
[So, you became the witch's dog to change the world?]
[Witches don't raise dogs. Although she raised the Red Ruby Cat, she even discarded it. She is fundamentally different from me. I just know how to use the poison she unleashed upon the world.]

[And the kid and Temar. I have experienced both, Lokia. I was the guardian dragon for both of them. There's no way you know the kid better than I do. The kid is different from Temar. He is... stronger.]
For Murakan, it was the first time he clearly acknowledged Jin over Temar. And it was a very unfamiliar thing for him. To put someone else above Temar.
[Well, we'll see about that when our descendant is put in a crucial moment. When something precious must be chosen, just one thing.]
